answer: Picture each agent's paid trades as edges in a graph. A Sybil farm forms an island: its fake agents trade densely with each other but only a few real bridge edges link it to honest agents. Verifiers send short random-walk voyages from trusted seeds; walks rarely cross those scarce bridges, so island identities collect little trust. To gain weight, the attacker must buy many genuine trades with honest agents, paying real fees for every bridge.
